title: Brick Anatomy
blurb: What lives inside GraphData — header, payload, Type.

chapters.title: Hello
chapters.text: The brick is a sandwich factory. Shell on the outside. Each box is bread plus filling. Little arrows point to kid boxes.
chapters.deep: Graph Data is a blob root: Graph Id, Root pointer, Inputs array, Outputs array, Root Nodes and Nodes hash maps of Node Union tags.

chapters.title: Shell
chapters.text: Outside: Graph Id stamps the backpack keys. Root is the start door. Inputs and Outputs are the labeled holes.
chapters.deep: Graph Input Data stores Variable Key and Burst Type Hash. Graph Output Data also stores a Blob Ptr to a Data Header that produces the value.

chapters.title: Box
chapters.text: Every node: bread is Type and Node Id. Filling is payload like Speed or score lists. Kids are blob pointers.
chapters.deep: Header is twelve-ish bytes: int Type, ulong Node Id. Payload is at address of header plus size of header. Same pattern for Execution and Data headers.

chapters.title: Doors
chapters.text: Robot reads Type, opens that door in the door book, runs the method, maybe follows more arrows, maybe writes the world.
chapters.deep: Data path special-cases Constant, Variable, Variable Set before Data Generated. Execution always goes through Execution Generated for non-default types.
